issues.reason: The distributing rule asserts at strength 0.9 that an arbitrary member of the kind iron_band reinforces this one named lantern, which the sentence does not state; the clause is neither a habitual/characteristic claim about iron bands nor a bare-kind relational generic (its object is a definite named individual), so the rule form puts a false claim into the KB.

new_gaps: A bare-plural subject in a present-tense STANDING-STATE clause with a definite specific object ('Iron bands reinforce the Stilllight Lantern') matches neither arm of the bare-plural split - it is not a past/dated/one-off occurrence, nor a habitual/characteristic claim about the kind - so the group-witness vs generic-rule choice is not legislated for it (only the group witness keeps every atom true).
defect_summary: The compliant form is the bare-plural group witness - (GroupOf sk_group_1 iron_band) plus one reinforce event with (Agent sk_reinforce_1 sk_group_1) and (Patient sk_reinforce_1 stilllight_lantern) - instead of an Implication ranging over the kind iron_band.
notes: The other three atoms are right: iron_band fuses with only the head genus exposed (iron is a noun modifier), and the kind word inside the name licenses (Member stilllight_lantern lantern).
